items.title: AMF human-in-the-loop adaptive shielding design and validation
items.abstract: To achieve optimal shielding performance of an active magnetic field (AMF), its shielding concept should be understood not as a hardware component but as an adaptive operational system. On a mission where radiation can vary quickly, resources will always be limited. Decisions can be made either automatically or under astronaut supervision. The idea behind the development of the AMF shielding described in this chapter is that of a human-in-the-loop (HITL) system in which astronauts' situational awareness, supervision, feedback from sensors, and the actuation of the magnetic field are integrated into a single adaptive protection scheme [1]. The development of the current chapter relies heavily on previous research related to the basic physical principles behind AMFs, trade-offs between shielding effectiveness and shielding material properties, secondary radiation, spacecraft charging, electromagnetic compatibility, and general considerations regarding risks within a larger system-of-systems architecture. The focus moves away from the technical feasibility of a subsystem toward a mission-oriented analysis of the potential of AMFs as radiation shields, including questions related to how effectively they will allow for mission adaptation while being compatible with astronaut decision-making under various conditions [2]. Three major threads run through the current chapter. First, this chapter explores the human-centered control architecture of AMF-based shielding, which describes how astronauts, sensors, supervising systems, and shielding subsystems work in conjunction to protect astronauts from space radiation [3]. Second, it studies the accumulated shielding effect as determined by time. In particular, the importance of cumulative dose reduction is emphasized, since shielding in deep space implies protection over the entire mission period, not just the instantaneous effectiveness of the shielding field [4]. Finally, the chapter provides an analysis of the energy consumption trade-off for different shielding modes [5].

items.title: An academic chatbot with hybrid retrieval and local large language models
items.abstract: Higher-education institutions devote a substantial share of their staff time to answering queries whose answers are already set out in institutional regulations. This paper presents the design and evaluation of an academic chatbot based on retrieval-augmented generation that lets users query those documents in natural language and receive grounded answers in Spanish. The system combines a structure-aware ingestion pipeline, a hybrid retriever that fuses dense semantic search and lexical search through reciprocal rank fusion, and a locally hosted large language model. A distinguishing goal is data sovereignty: every component runs on institutional hardware, so no data is sent to external services. Quality is evaluated with the RAGAS framework over five regulatory documents: the corpus-wide set attains a global score of 0.90, with faithfulness of 0.97. The acceptance criterion is not met, however, under its conjunctive reading: answer relevancy stays below its threshold across all sets, and p95 latency reaches 6.47 seconds against a 5-second target. Quality further degrades on long, heavily cross-referenced regulations. A contrast questionnaire administered to nineteen users places the perception index at 3.64 out of 5 and exposes a relevant discrepancy: only 57.9% agree that the system does not produce fabricated information, against the faithfulness the automatic judge assigns it.

items.title: An agentic multi-drone framework for autonomous multi-accident detection, reasoning, and response
items.abstract: Rapid and effective response to highway accidents is critical for reducing response delays and improving situational awareness. In this study, we present an agentic multi-drone, end-to-end incident management framework, developed and validated in the Gazebo simulation environment, in which specialized planning, coordination, perception, scene-description, and dispatch agents communicate through ROS/MAVROS and MQTT interfaces. A simulated emergency call transcript is processed by a GPT-4o mini-based planning agent to extract incident coordinates and mission intent, which the coordination agent resolves into an optimal drone-to-incident allocation. Up to four autonomous drones, each managed via MAVROS and ArduPilot, navigate under GUIDED mode to their assigned sites, where a custom-trained YOLOv11n perception agent performs real-time accident and fire recognition on live aerial imagery. Detected events trigger a fine-tuned BLIP-2 description agent, which converts visual evidence into structured natural-language incident reports. When multiple reports correspond to the same incident, confidence-prioritized fusion selects the highest-confidence view as the primary description and supplements it with non-duplicated salient information from secondary views. A Piper TTS-based dispatch agent then converts these summaries into audio alerts and autonomously routes them to the nearest rescue center based on drone proximity. The description agent was fine-tuned on 1,783 image–caption pairs derived from the curated incident dataset, with reference captions generated using moondream2, holding its visual encoder and Q-Former frozen to preserve pre-trained feature representations, and evaluated on a held-out set of 254 samples using BLEU-4, ROUGE-L, METEOR, CIDEr, and SPICE. Results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed modular agentic architecture for autonomous multi-incident perception, reasoning, and coordinated drone-based emergency response in the evaluated four-drone, four-incident simulation configuration. The framework provides a basis for future validation in larger-scale and real-world emergency-response scenarios.

items.title: An expert routing-driven graph framework from tongue multi-task features to liver fibrosis prediction
items.abstract: Liver fibrosis is a global health concern where early detection is crucial for timely intervention. Traditional Chinese Medicine tongue diagnosis offers a promising non-invasive assessment, but suffers from inter-observer variability and subjective interpretation. Current artificial intelligence approaches focus on binary classification without revealing tongue features influencing diagnosis, limiting clinical utility. To address these challenges, we propose two key artificial intelligence innovations: (1) Hierarchical Kolmogorov–Arnold Network-based Adaptive Multi-task Experts, a novel multi-task learning architecture with adaptive quota routing that dynamically determines expert allocation based on sample complexity, solving the negative transfer problem; (2) Dynamic Tongue Relationship Graph Convolutional Network, a graph neural network that transforms expert selection patterns into patient-specific relationship graphs, enabling personalized modeling of attribute interactions. These artificial intelligence contributions advance the state-of-the-art in multi-task learning and dynamic graph construction for heterogeneous data, representing our core contributions at the artificial intelligence algorithmic level. As the engineering application of these artificial intelligence innovations, we develop Tongue Network with Dynamic Graph Relationship Learning, a non-invasive and interpretable framework based on tongue images that identifies seven critical tongue attributes and models their interrelationships for liver fibrosis risk screening in Traditional Chinese Medicine-based hepatology practice. Our method achieves 0.751 accuracy and 0.767 area under the curve, with 0.07 and 0.08 improvements over state-of-the-art graph neural networks and multimodal approaches. The framework offers visualizable classifications and relationship structures, providing insights into tongue features and liver fibrosis risk assessment. Codes are available at https://github.com/MedAI-UAIX/TongueNet-DGRL .

items.title: An intelligent decision-making model for accelerating green manufacturing adoption in automotive, electronics, and textile industries
items.abstract: Abstract Manufacturing industry is being increasingly forced to go green without compromising on the efficiency and effectiveness of their operations. This paper discusses an artificial intelligence based approach for encouraging the adoption of green practices in the manufacturing industries. Green manufacturing is an essential way of attaining environmental sustainability. However, the adoption of green manufacturing is still a challenge owing to the problem of reconciling the economic objectives with the environmental requirements. The integration of machine learning and green manufacturing results into a decision support system. The AI model designed utilizes predictive analytics, neural networks, and optimization algorithms for the identification of green manufacturing opportunities and for the formulation of strategies for their implementation. The data used comes from 85 manufacturing plants of the automotive, electronics, and textile industries, which proves the effectiveness of the model. The results show that AI-assisted green manufacturing reaches up to 27% less energy use, 22% material waste reduction, and 25% lower carbon footprint so far comparing with the traditional methods. The model is going to be a source of support and practical advice for the manufacturers, who are willing to be environmentally responsible and perform operatively, thus, the research will add to and share the existing academic knowledge of sustainable manufacturing along with the industrial part of the practice.

items.title: An Organizational Socialization Support System for Newly Hired Research and Development Employees in High-Tech Enterprises: A Case Study of Mentorship at G Automobile Group
items.abstract: In high-tech research and development (R&D) contexts, where artificial intelligence (AI)-powered tools and digital collaboration platforms are becoming increasingly prevalent, the learning and integration pathways of newly hired R&D employees are undergoing structural changes. Mentorship has emerged as a key mechanism supporting organizational socialization and innovation. This study examines the role of mentorship as a core mechanism in integrating internal digital platforms and cross-departmental resources to construct a systematic organizational socialization support network. Adopting a qualitative, cross-sectional single-case study strategy, this study collected data through semi-structured interviews and internal archival documents and analyzed the data using directed content analysis. This study finds that G Automobile Group embeds mentorship into its “180-Day Transformation Program,” thereby forming a closed-loop development system through growth planning, dynamic feedback, and regular reviews. By combining contextualized on-the-job mentoring with resource-based self-directed learning, mentorship facilitates the transformation of tacit knowledge into job competence. A hierarchical mentoring system, knowledge accumulation through digital platforms, and cross-departmental resource integration further enhance the effectiveness of newcomer socialization. The study also finds that mentors serve dual roles as supporters and evaluators. Transparent standards and clear communication processes are required to reduce the risk of negative mentoring experiences. The novelty of this study lies in conceptualizing mentorship not merely as a dyadic support relationship but as a digitally embedded organizational socialization support system that integrates formal mentoring, informal resource flows, AI-enabled tools, and cross-departmental collaboration.

items.title: An unmanned aerial vehicle-assisted visual measurement framework for forest road condition assessment with overlapping distress quantification
items.abstract: Routine forest-road maintenance is essential for road safety, accessibility, and serviceability, yet current inspections remain labor-intensive. Existing visual methods usually quantify pavement distresses independently, which may introduce area-estimation errors and affect condition assessment when multiple distresses spatially overlap. To address this engineering challenge, this study proposes an engineering artificial intelligence framework integrating Transformer-based semantic segmentation and diffusion-based data augmentation for unmanned aerial vehicle-assisted multi-distress measurement, overlapping-distress quantification, and forest-road condition assessment. This framework incorporates a segmentation model that converts aerial images into pixel-level distress masks for area measurement. The segmentation model employs a dynamic-gated convolutional backbone to integrate local textures with global context and a frequency-modulated spatial attention decoder to enhance small-scale and weakly visible distresses. A two-stage overlapping-distress identification strategy is developed to localize overlapping regions, identify their constituent distress categories, and support overlap-aware area quantification and condition assessment. A multi-condition guided diffusion model is further introduced to enrich inspection-image diversity, and a Forest Road Daily Inspection dataset is constructed for model training and evaluation. For engineering assessment, a Forest Pavement Condition Index is developed by incorporating measured areas of multiple distress types and overlapping regions, enabling section-level condition evaluation and maintenance prioritization. Experiments on the constructed forest-road inspection dataset and a public benchmark demonstrate that the proposed segmentation model improves multi-distress segmentation, overlapping-region identification, and measurement-oriented condition assessment, supporting its potential for forest-road condition measurement and maintenance-oriented assessment under the tested conditions.

items.title: Analog RF Computing for Integrated Data and AI Flows Over Wireless Networks
items.abstract: Many resource-constrained edge devices require artificial intelligence (AI) services but are not powerful enough to store or execute neural networks (NNs). Analog radio frequency (RF) computing addresses this limitation by letting a base station (BS) multicast a waveform encoding NN weights to different clients. Each client then multiplies the received weight-encoded waveform with its locally generated input-encoded waveform through a passive mixer in its RF frontend, thereby realizing the matrix-vector multiplications (MVMs) needed for AI inference with an extremely low power and memory requirement. This can enable telecom operators to provide AI inference services to the edge devices connected to their networks. In practice, however, this multicast AI flow must share the spectrum, power, and spatial resources with other data flows. This paper considers a multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) downlink scenario and studies the resulting relative aggregate data rate reduction from integrating the multicast AI flow with the unicast data flows. We formulate a joint beamforming problem for the data and AI flows to maximize the aggregate data rate subject to computing accuracy, client energy, total power, and hardware-related constraints. We develop a weighted minimum mean-square error (WMMSE)-based algorithm to solve the problem. Numerical results based on 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) channels show that the relative aggregate data rate reduction from integrating an AI flow with data flows is below 5% in representative settings. This indicates that telecom operators can use analog RF computing to provide edge AI services while providing data communication services simultaneously.

items.title: Analysis of the Influence of the Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on Students' Critical Thinking Abilities in Learning
items.abstract: This study examines how Artificial Intelligence (AI) use affects students' critical thinking skills in learning. The study uses a quantitative, explanatory research design. The study population consisted of students in the Economics Education Study Program who used AI-based applications for learning. The study collected data through a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire from 64 respondents who met the research criteria. The researchers analyzed the data using validity and reliability tests, assumption tests, and simple linear regression in SPSS. The results show that using AI has a positive and significant effect on students' critical thinking skills. The t-test yielded t = 4.670 (p = 0.000), and the regression coefficient was 0.431. The R-square value of 0.260 indicates that AI use explains 26% of the variation in students' critical thinking skills, while other factors account for the remaining 74%. These findings suggest that appropriate AI use can support students' ability to analyze, evaluate, and solve problems.

items.title: Analysis of the potential profile and influencing factors of health behavior protection motivation in patients with unruptured intracranial aneurysms based on protection motivation theory
items.abstract: Background Rupture of unruptured intracranial aneurysms (UIA) is the third leading cause of morbidity and mortality from cerebrovascular disease, with a disability rate as high as 36–58%; health behaviors are crucial for reducing the risk of rupture. Protection Motivation Theory serves as an effective framework for explaining the formation of health behaviors; however, there is currently a lack of analyses on the latent categories of protection motivation for health behaviors among UIA patients both domestically and internationally, and in-depth exploration of population heterogeneity and intrinsic motivation has been neglected. Based on Protection Motivation Theory, this study explores the overall level and dimensional characteristics of protection motivation for health behaviors among UIA patients, analyzes its latent profiles and influencing factors, and provides a reference for clinical stratified management and personalized interventions. Methods From July to December 2025, a convenience sample of 300 UIA patients meeting the inclusion criteria was recruited from a Grade A tertiary hospital in Jiangxi Province for a clinical survey. A self-designed general demographic questionnaire, the UIA Patient Health Behavior Protective Motivation Scale, and the Health Promotion Lifestyle Scale II (HPLP-II) were used to assess the current status of health behavior protective motivation, health-promoting lifestyles, and their relationship among UIA patients. This study employed latent profile analysis (LPA) to identify latent profiles among UIA patients. One-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) was used to compare differences in general demographic data and disease-related scores across latent profiles. Chi-square tests and Fisher’s exact test were used for categorical variables. Pearson correlation analysis was used to examine the relationship between protection motivation and health-promoting behaviors. Multinomial logistic regression was used to investigate the factors influencing these latent profiles. Results The results of this study showed that the total score for health behavior protection motivation among UIA patients was (81.96 ± 15.41) points, and the total score for health behavior promotion was (126.83 ± 30.78) points. The total score for health behavior protection motivation was positively correlated with the total scores of the HPLP-II and the HPLP-II ( r = 0.73, p < 0.001),and the total scores of each dimension were positively correlated with the total score for health behavior promotion ( p < 0.001). One-way ANOVA revealed significant differences in HPLP-II total scores across the three latent profiles ( F (2, 297) = 136.459, p < 0.001). Chi-square tests showed significant differences in educational level, sleep quality, smoking, alcohol consumption, and comorbid chronic diseases across the three groups ( χ 2 = 7.693–60.171, df = 2–4, all p < 0.05). This study identified three latent profiles of protective motivation: the low protective motivation group (21.0%), the moderate protective motivation group (53.0%), and the high protective motivation group (26.0%). Multinomial logistic regression analysis showed that educational level (OR = 6.997, 95% CI: 2.053–23.850), sleep quality (OR = 5.069, 95% CI: 1.644–15.626), and HPLP-II total score (OR = 1.078, 95% CI: 1.051–1.105) were facilitators for the moderate group, while smoking (OR = 0.357, 95% CI: 0.138–0.928) and alcohol consumption (OR = 0.103, 95% CI: 0.053–0.201) were barriers. For the high group, educational level (OR = 8.010, 95% CI: 1.855–34.597) and HPLP-II total score (OR = 1.147, 95% CI: 1.113–1.183) were facilitators, while alcohol consumption (OR = 0.101, 95% CI: 0.047–0.218) was a barrier. Conclusion The total scores for health behavior protection and motivation, and the total HPLP-II scores, among UIA patients were generally moderate. Furthermore, health behavior protection motivation exhibited heterogeneity and could be classified into three distinct latent profiles. Clinically, personalized intervention plans can be developed based on the characteristics and latent profiles of patients, with the aim of enhancing patients’ levels of health behavior protection motivation, improving health-promoting behaviors, reducing the risk of aneurysm rupture, and improving long-term disease prognosis.

items.title: Anticipated Acceptance of AI-Proactive Smart Sofas: A Value–Reactance Dual-Pathway Model
items.abstract: Proactive AI can make domestic products more responsive while raising concerns about unwanted intervention, control, and privacy. This study examines anticipated acceptance of AI-proactive smart sofas through a value–reactance framework. A theory-guided exploratory sequential mixed-methods design combinedinterviews with 10 prospective users and a scenario-based survey of 401 valid cases. PLS-SEM showed that perceived AI proactivity was positively associated with perceived usefulness and perceived intrusiveness, although the usefulness-related coefficient was substantially larger. Perceived usefulness was positively associated with AI trust and behavioral intention, whereas perceived intrusiveness was positively associated with psychological reactance, which was negatively associated with AI trust and behavioral intention. Privacy sensitivity positively moderated the intrusiveness–reactance association, although the interaction was small. Because participants evaluated a hypothetical product rather than interacting with an actual sofa, behavioral intention is interpreted as anticipated acceptance rather than observed adoption. The findings highlight user control, transparency, and privacy as design considerations.

items.title: Are We Really Measuring Forgetting? Pitfalls in Evaluating Machine Unlearning for Multimodal LLMs
items.abstract: As machine unlearning for multimodal large language models (MLLMs) rapidly advances, rigorous evaluation of its effectiveness becomes increasingly important. However, existing benchmarks largely inherit evaluation protocols from text-only unlearning and overlook the unique challenges of unlearning in multimodal settings. In this work, we identify three major pitfalls that may lead to misleading conclusions: the lack of heldout evaluation to distinguish genuine concept-wise forgetting from instance-wise overfitting, the reliance on synthetic, fine-tuned knowledge rather than real-world knowledge acquired during pre-training, and unfair method comparisons caused by applying the same training settings to different unlearning methods. To address these challenges, we introduce GEMMU (Generalizable Evaluation for Multimodal Machine Unlearning), a benchmark built on real-world knowledge and a principled evaluation protocol. Re-evaluating representative unlearning methods under GEMMU reveals substantial generalization gaps and challenges conclusions drawn from previous benchmarks. Our findings highlight the importance of rigorous evaluation for advancing multimodal machine unlearning and provide guidelines for future benchmark design.

items.title: Are women cryopreserving enough oocytes for fertility preservation? A probabilistic model integrating AI-based oocyte morphology and age-dependent euploidy
items.abstract: Abstract STUDY QUESTION How many mature oocytes are biologically required to achieve at least three euploid blastocysts, by maternal age and AI-derived oocyte quality, and how does this estimate compare with real-world oocyte yields in elective fertility preservation? SUMMARY ANSWER Required oocyte numbers rise steeply with advancing maternal age and decreasing AI-derived oocyte quality, and the median number cryopreserved per fertility preservation cycle falls progressively below estimated requirements, by 12- to 30-fold in women older than 40 years. WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY Elective oocyte cryopreservation is increasingly used to preserve future reproductive potential, but counselling typically relies on uniform age-based oocyte targets that do not account for inter-individual variability in oocyte biological competence. Although AI-based oocyte assessment has shown promise as an objective adjunct to morphological evaluation, no biologically integrated framework has been used to translate AI-derived oocyte quality into a quantitative requirement-versus-yield comparison in fertility preservation. STUDY DESIGN, SIZE, DURATION Retrospective cohort study with probabilistic modelling of blastulation and euploidy, using three datasets from a single private university-affiliated IVF centre. Model development used 13,782 mature oocytes from 1,625 autologous ICSI cycles (1,020 patients, 2021–2024) and 3,325 biopsied embryos with conclusive PGT-A results (857 patients). External validation was performed in 1,948 oocytes from 333 ovum donation cycles in 271 donors (2020–2024). Real-world application used 1,647 elective fertility preservation cycles in 1,100 patients between 2012 and 2024. PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS, SETTING, METHODS Each oocyte was scored using a commercially available artificial-intelligence image-analysis system that assigns a 0–10 oocyte quality score. Blastulation and euploidy were modelled by logistic regression with cluster-robust standard errors. The integrated probabilistic framework computed the minimum number of mature oocytes required to obtain at least three euploid blastocysts at a probability of 90% or greater, by maternal age category and tertile of AI-derived oocyte quality score. Model-derived requirements were compared with the median number of oocytes actually cryopreserved per fertility preservation cycle. MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE Blastulation increased with higher AI-derived oocyte quality score (OR 1.19 per point, 95% CI 1.18–1.21; P < 0.001) and decreased with maternal age (OR 0.94 per year, 95% CI 0.93–0.96; P < 0.001); the oocyte quality effect was externally validated in donors (OR 1.11 per point, 95% CI 1.08–1.14). Euploidy declined non-linearly with age, from 68.6% (<30 years) to 19.3% (>40 years). Estimated mature-oocyte requirements ranged from 9 (95% CI 8–11) at < 30 years with high AI-derived oocyte quality to 121 (104–146) at > 40 years with low AI-derived oocyte quality. The median number cryopreserved per cycle decreased from 8.3 at < 30 to 4.0 at > 40 years and fell progressively below estimated requirements; in women older than 40 years the observed yield was 12- to 30-fold below the estimated requirement. LIMITATIONS, REASONS FOR CAUTION Blastulation and euploidy probabilities were derived from autologous ICSI cycles in patients with infertility-related indications; extrapolation to elective fertility preservation candidates assumes that per-oocyte biological competence, conditional on age and AI-derived quality, is transportable across populations. The probabilistic framework assumes conditional independence between blastulation and euploidy. The model estimates oocyte requirements for euploid blastocyst formation but does not directly model implantation, clinical pregnancy, or live birth. WIDER IMPLICATIONS OF THE FINDINGS The divergence between observed yields and model-derived requirements is best interpreted not as a deficiency in retrieval practice but as an individualised benchmark. Integrating AI-based oocyte assessment with age-specific euploidy probabilities may support more personalised, biologically informed counselling, expectation-setting, and care planning, particularly for women considering oocyte cryopreservation after the mid-thirties. FUNDING This research did not receive any specific grant from public, commercial, or not-for-profit funding agencies. DISCLOSURES J.F. and P.M. are employees of Future Fertility, the developer of the artificial-intelligence oocyte-scoring system used in this study. The remaining authors declare no competing interests. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER N/A

items.title: ARIA: Runtime Inspection and Amendment for Multi-Agent Systems
items.abstract: In LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS), a local mistake can propagate as other agents build on it, turning a correctable error into a failed task. Diagnosing completed runs or repeatedly re-executing them to search for corrections does not provide a learned policy for intervening while execution is still in progress. We present Agent Runtime Inspection and Amendment (ARIA), a framework for learning when and how to repair ongoing multi-agent executions. Our key intuition is to turn execution-verified repairs into reusable supervision, moving repair search into data construction and training so that a learned model can intervene at runtime without repeatedly testing alternatives. First, we collect over 24{,}000 successful and failed trajectories across four multi-agent frameworks, six benchmarks, and eight host models. From these trajectories, we construct the ARIA dataset, to our knowledge the first large-scale dataset pairing failed multi-agent trajectories with execution-verified repairs. It contains 3{,}953 verified repair pairs, each specifying what went wrong, where to intervene, and how execution should continue. Then, we develop the ARIA framework for MAS-agnostic runtime inspection and amendment, designed to integrate with any MAS that exposes execution trajectories and supports continuation replacement. Using verified repairs as training examples, we teach a compact model to recognize when intervention is needed and how to correct an ongoing run. The aim is to learn repair strategies that apply to related failures in new configurations, rather than merely reproduce individual corrections. Finally, the trained ARIA model demonstrates strong repair performance in both post-hoc and runtime settings, with generalization to unseen frameworks and host models. Our code is available at https://github.com/LabRAI/ARIA.

items.title: Articulation Upper Bounds for Language Models
items.abstract: Language captures only a subset of the perceptions, intuitions and intents that form meaning between speakers. What, then, are the limits of language? We take steps towards measuring this in LLMs as follows: for a set of concepts, we measure how well each concept can be transmitted between two LLMs as their capabilities scale. This requires novel measurement tools: (1) optimal messages: we introduce a prompt optimization algorithm that beats existing algorithms by up to 14% on benchmarks and accurately estimates prompt upper bounds. (2) A transmission measure: the sender is asked to label text; the receiver then tries to recover the sender's prompt, and recovery is measured; we find this correlates strongly with human label error. With these measures, we use observational scaling laws to study how transmissibility of a concept, conveyed with optimal messages, increases as transmitter and receiver capacity grows: does it asymptote below or above a threshold? Measuring 1.2k concepts in eight domains, we find concepts that (a) can be fully articulated; these concepts usually depend on local patterns, e.g. "joke ends with surprise"; (b) might be articulated by future, stronger models; these rely on whole-text structural patterns, e.g. "story's worldbuilding coherence"; (c) concepts that face articulability limits; these concepts' meaning, we find, is tied to identity and social-group awareness, e.g. "comic voice". Interesting, these same concepts are not all challenging for humans: humans have moderate-to-high levels of agreement in 76% of concepts that LLMs struggle with; articulation limits, we find, are executor relative. Finally, we characterize the nature of improvement in each case: while recoverable concepts can be articulated through definitions and explanations, irrecoverable concepts cannot be transmitted, even with examples, and might require novel learning mechanisms.

items.title: Artificial intelligence and venture capital: Revisiting sourcing, selection, and nurturing activities
items.abstract: Abstract Research Summary Venture capital (VC) is an information‐intensive form of entrepreneurial finance conducted under extreme uncertainty. Investors must originate promising opportunities, select ventures with sparse and strategically disclosed information, and monitor and support firms after investment. Prior research documents both formal mechanisms (e.g., staged financing, syndication) and informal mechanisms built on referrals, reputation, and constant interaction. Geographic and social proximity enable these mechanisms by lowering the cost of obtaining contextual information and coordinating action. We develop a mechanism‐based account of how data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) reconfigure this established model. Our framework yields propositions on geographic dispersion in sourcing, portfolio selection, and the distinct effects of AI on monitoring versus value‐added support. It also identifies boundary conditions associated with institutional setting and heterogeneous AI adoption. Managerial Summary For venture capital firms, AI is not a single tool and adoption is not a binary choice. A fund may use data systems to identify founders, machine‐learning models to organize deal flow, generative AI to summarize diligence materials, or analytics to monitor portfolio companies. Each application changes a different part of the VC process. In sourcing, AI can widen the funnel beyond warm introductions and local ecosystems, especially in sectors such as software and e‐commerce where hiring, product, and customer signals are visible. In selection, AI can make diligence faster and more consistent, but models trained on past investments may favor ventures that resemble previously funded companies and may miss novel opportunities for which historical analogues are weak. In post‐investment activity, continuous operational data can partly replace physical presence for monitoring, while value‐add support such as customer introductions, recruiting, strategy advice, and founder coaching remain relationship‐intensive. The practical implication is a task‐level approach: automate codifiable search and processing, retain independent human judgment where uncertainty is fundamental, and use AI to strengthen rather than erode trusted investor–founder relationships. Funds also face organizational choices about building proprietary infrastructure, buying external tools, or combining the two. The appropriate configuration depends on data access, strategy, scale, and the activity in which the fund seeks advantage.

items.title: Artificial intelligence attitudes, presenteeism, and work engagement among nurses: a structural equation modeling approach
items.abstract: Introduction The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into healthcare has transformed clinical practice, yet the psychological mechanisms linking nurses’ AI attitudes to their occupational functioning remain insufficiently understood, particularly regarding the role of presenteeism as a potential explanatory pathway. This study aimed to examine the relationships among nurses’ attitudes toward AI, presenteeism, and work engagement, and to test the mediating role of presenteeism within a Job Demands-Resources framework. Methods A cross-sectional correlational design was employed, with data collected from 806 hospital nurses across Saudi Arabia and Egypt using the AI Attitude Scale for Nurses, the Presenteeism Scale in Nursing, and the Utrecht Work Engagement Scale. Data were analyzed via structural equation modeling with bootstrapped mediation testing (2,000 resamples) and multi-group invariance analysis. Results Following the exclusion of four multivariate outliers, the final analytic sample comprised 802 nurses. The hypothesized model demonstrated good fit (CFI = 0.981, RMSEA = 0.068). AI attitude significantly and negatively predicted presenteeism (β = −0.366, p < 0.001) and positively predicted work engagement (β = 0.436, p < 0.001), while presenteeism negatively predicted engagement (β = −0.250, p < 0.001). Presenteeism significantly and partially mediated this relationship (indirect β = 0.092, 95% CI [0.065, 0.123]), with the model explaining approximately 33.2% of variance in engagement. Configural, metric, and structural invariance was confirmed across Egyptian and Saudi nurses. Discussion These associational findings suggest that more favorable AI attitudes are linked to lower presenteeism and stronger engagement, offering preliminary guidance for nursing management and healthcare digitalization policies pending longitudinal confirmation.

items.abstract: The proliferation of wearable Internet of Things (IoT) devices has introduced novel opportunities for continuous and objective monitoring of individuals engaged in meditation and controlled breathing practices.This study presents an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven framework for assessing the physiological and psychological effects associated with Daoist meditation and breathing techniques through real-time multimodal wearable sensor data analysis.The proposed framework integrates multiple physiological and behavioral parameters, including heartrate variability (HRV), respiratory rate (RR), blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), skin temperature (ST), electrodermal activity (EDA), sleep patterns, and physical movement (PM).A comprehensive data-processing pipeline is developed, incorporating signal filtering, artefact removal, normalization, multithreaded segmentation, and feature extraction across heterogeneous sensing modalities.Machine-learning (ML) and deep-learning (DL) approaches are employed to model complex relationships between physiological responses and meditative states.The framework supports multiple analytical tasks, including meditation stage classification, breathing pattern recognition, relaxation-level assessment, and longitudinal monitoring of physiological variations.Statistical and computational analyses are performed to evaluate differences among resting conditions, controlled breathing sessions, and distinct meditation stages, with particular emphasis on autonomic nervous system (ANS) activity and stress-related physiological indicators.To enhance model interpretability, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) techniques are incorporated to identify key physiological features contributing to predictive outcomes.Furthermore, the framework enables real-time personalized feedback by generating adaptive recommendations based on individual biometric characteristics and historical practice patterns.The integration of Daoist contemplative practices with wearable sensing technologies, artificial intelligence, and real-time analytics provides a novel approach for scientifically evaluating traditional mind-body practices.The proposed framework offers potential applications in digital health monitoring, stress management, personalized wellness systems, and the development of intelligent platforms for individualized contemplative practice optimization.

items.title: Artificial intelligence driven transformation of 3D concrete printing in architecture: a systematic review
items.abstract: The combination of artificial intelligence (AI) with 3D concrete printing (3DCP) is becoming an important approach in architectural design and construction. AI techniques are increasingly being utilized for design generation, material optimization, and assessment in 3DCP. This paper presents a systematic literature review of AI applications in architectural additive manufacturing, following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines and focusing on the use of machine learning, deep learning, artificial neural networks, and computer vision across different stages of the 3DCP workflow. Peer-reviewed studies indexed in the Web of Science and Scopus databases were analyzed. The review revealed three key research areas: AI-driven design and form generation, optimization of material and structural performance, and fabrication monitoring. The findings highlight the potential of AI to reduce material usage, improve printability, and automate quality control assessments, while also identifying challenges related to data availability, standardization, and real-world implementation in 3DCP.

items.title: Artificial intelligence for astrobiology investigations (AI2): an open-source graphical user interface
items.abstract: A growing number of studies in astrobiological research have utilized and shown the potential in applied machine learning. However, the number of these studies are still quite limited. Furthermore, educators, students, and researchers often do not have the time and/or resources for developing machine learning knowledge and skills. To facilitate the use of applied machine learning for astrobiology, we developed an open-source and freely available web-based graphical user interface (GUI) for teaching and developing machine learning models called Artificial Intelligence for Astrobiology Investigations (AI 2 ) . Our project enables educators, students, and researchers to make use of explainable machine learning models most amenable to tabular (i.e.csv files) astrobiology datasets. The application is an interactive tool and serves as an entry point for educators, students, and researchers who are novices in machine learning. By providing an easy to follow and standardized machine learning workflow, the GUI highlights how certain machine learning approaches work, and how to reliably utilize machine learning Furthermore, the application can serve as a means of rapid prototyping of machine learning models, with or without the need for technical expertise, thus freeing up time for researchers to investigate and explore their data. Accordingly, the AI 2 project aims to serve as a stepping stone towards more advanced implementation of applied machine learning by building the foundation and intuition necessary for technical expertise.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence for Cardiac Ischemia Detection: A Review of Biosensor, Biomarker, and Imaging Applications
items.abstract: Ischemic heart disease is the leading cause of global mortality, yet accurate and timely detection remains constrained by incomplete signal capture, noise, operator dependence, and imperfect reference standards. Artificial intelligence (AI) may enhance cardiovascular sensing by extracting latent diagnostic information from routinely acquired signals. This narrative review examines AI-enabled approaches to ischemia detection across three sensing modalities: the electrocardiogram as a bioelectric sensor, cardiac troponin as a biochemical marker, and cardiac imaging technologies (echocardiography, computed tomography, magnetic resonance, and nuclear imaging) as structural and functional sensors. For each modality, we evaluate the sensing pipeline, the reference standards, the endpoint actually measured (from acute coronary occlusion to functional ischemia), and reported performance metrics, separating diagnostic accuracy from effects on clinical workflow, patient outcomes, and cost. We also discuss emerging directions, including foundation models and multimodal fusion, together with translational challenges such as limited prospective validation, regulatory hurdles, and uncertain cost-effectiveness. Most evidence comes from retrospective, frequently single-center studies of diagnostic performance; few studies have measured effects on workflow, and fewer still on patient outcomes or cost. Routine clinical adoption will require prospective multicenter trials, standardized performance benchmarks, and evidence of clinical and economic benefit.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence for Early Prediction of Intracranial Hypertension: From Single-Centre Development to Multicentre Validation
items.abstract: Abstract Background Raised intracranial pressure is one of the most severe secondary insults after traumatic brain injury. Recognising physiological patterns before they progress to dangerous intracranial pressure elevations could enable preventive rather than reactive interventions. In our previous Uppsala single-centre study, an XGBoost machine learning model showed high discriminative performance for prediction of imminent intracranial pressure insults. The model identifies short-term physiological trajectories associated with imminent threshold crossing rather than predicting independent future clinical events. Whether these results are generalisable across centres is unknown. The aim was therefore to evaluate whether the XGBoost model trained on an Uppsala dataset maintains similar performance when applied to a multicentre TBI cohort - The CENTER-TBI High-Resolution ICU cohort. Methods The XGBoost model trained on the Uppsala high frequency traumatic brain injury cohort was externally validated using data from the multicentre CENTER-TBI cohort. Minute-level averages of intracranial pressure and invasive arterial blood pressure were used to predict the onset of an intracranial pressure insult within 30 min on the basis of a 4h historical window. A bidirectional validation design was applied and performance was assessed using multiple metrics. Results The cohorts comprised 602 patients from Uppsala and 255 patients from the CENTER-TBI database. When trained on the Uppsala cohort and tested on CENTER-TBI, the model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 97.4%, sensitivity of 93.8%, and specificity of 98.6%. Training on CENTER-TBI and testing on the Uppsala dataset yielded an AUROC of 96.1%, sensitivity of 81.2%, and specificity of 98.7%. Balanced accuracy exceeded 88% in both validation directions. Conclusions The XGBoost model retained high performance under external multicentre validation, indicating that pre-insult physiological patterns preceding increased intracranial pressure are shared across cohorts. Differences in sensitivity between validation directions were observed and may reflect cohort characteristics or dataset size. These findings support the need for local evaluation before clinical implementation.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence for Movement Analysis in Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Scoping Review of Gait, Stereotyped Motor Movements, and Motor Behaviors
items.abstract: Motor differences are increasingly recognized as relevant early markers of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), although they are not part of the core diagnostic criteria. Recent advances in computer vision, pose estimation, and machine learning have enabled the quantitative analysis of movement patterns, particularly stereotyped motor movements (SMMs) and gait deviations. This scoping review examines recent artificial intelligence approaches for analyzing motor and movement patterns in individuals with ASD, with particular emphasis on stereotyped motor movements (SMMs) and gait-related differences. The reviewed studies used 2D and 3D pose estimation, conventional machine learning algorithms, and deep learning models to extract movement features from video, skeletal, depth, and sensor-based data. The included studies addressed different outcomes, including ASD versus TD classification, SMM and repetitive-behavior detection, gait abnormality classification or characterization, motor phenotype assessment, and movement measurement or validation. Because these studies examined different tasks and used different performance metrics, their results cannot be directly compared. However, small or private datasets, heterogeneous protocols, and limited external validation restrict cross-study comparison and clinical generalizability. Overall, the current evidence supports technical movement analysis rather than validated clinical ASD screening or diagnosis.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence for Payer Population Health Risk stratification, care gaps, and intervention prioritization in chronic care
items.abstract: Payer population health requires a distinction between predicting an adverse outcome, identifying a documented care gap, and selecting a response. We organized public evidence on computational approaches to these functions in chronic care, with Latin America as the context of interest and international studies retained as a separate comparator layer. A structured directed review used a July 16, 2026 search and October 2 targeted source verification, rather than a comprehensive update. We interpreted peer-reviewed research, other academic reports, and official institutional descriptions according to their tasks, accessible content, and evaluation maturity. International studies demonstrated retrospective modeling with administrative data, while care-sequence analyses and non-AI workflows illustrated different approaches to assessing gaps and organizing follow-up. Internal validation, external cohort validation, prospective utility, intervention effects, and routine implementation were treated separately. Official cases described programs or governance, not independently established AI effectiveness. The retrieved Latin American sources provide methodological and non-AI operational context, not evidence of prospectively validated payer AI or demonstrated intervention benefit. Authors' recommendations emphasize explicit outcome definitions, data and subgroup checks, human response design, and staged evaluation before operational use. External evidence supports an evaluation agenda; it does not establish local transferability, clinical benefit, or cost savings.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence for Risk Prediction in Perioperative Cancer Surgery: a Narrative Review
items.abstract: Abstract Purpose of Review Artificial intelligence (AI) particularly machine learning (ML) are increasingly used to predict perioperative risk in patients undergoing major cancer surgery. This narrative review aims to orient perioperative clinicians to contemporary AI-based predictive modelling, critically appraise the current evidence, and examine how these tools can be integrated into clinical decision-making within a Learning Health System framework. Recent Findings Recent studies show promise for AI-based prediction of perioperative outcomes compared with traditional tools in selected settings. However, performance gains are variable. Many models lack explainability, external validation, calibration assessment, or evidence of real-world clinical impact. Summary AI-based predictive models show promise for perioperative risk stratification in cancer surgery, but require external validation, interpretability, and links to actionable clinical pathways to be rigorously established. Future research should prioritise prospective evaluation, equity, workflow integration, and implementation science to translate predictive accuracy into meaningful clinical benefit.

items.title: Artificial intelligence in cardiovascular imaging and electrocardiography
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning, is reshaping cardiovascular imaging and electrocardiography (ECG) by enabling automated acquisition support, quantification, disease detection, and risk prediction. Yet, high retrospective accuracy does not by itself establish transportability or clinical benefit. This narrative review first outlines the AI development lifecycle, with emphasis on data and label quality, architecture selection, patient-level data partitioning, calibration, external validation, and prospective evaluation. It then critically examines representative advances in ECG, echocardiography, cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), cardiac computed tomography (CT), and nuclear cardiology. Particular attention is given to three rapidly evolving areas: AI-enhanced ECG, video- and vision-language echocardiography, and volumetric CT and CMR analysis. We compare convolutional, transformer-based, hybrid, and generative approaches; summarize explainable-AI methods, including gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM), SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), integrated gradients, and occlusion testing; and analyze failure modes arising from label, sampling, demographic, device, and temporal bias. Quantitative examples show that performance can deteriorate across institutions, demographic groups, and acquisition settings despite apparently strong internal validation. Future progress will depend on prospective workflow-based trials, multimodal foundation models with transparent benchmarks, lifecycle governance and regulation, and continuous post-deployment surveillance.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Eye Disease: A Systematic Review of Screening, Diagnosis, Prognosis, Treatment-Response Prediction, and Clinical Decision Support
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Artificial intelligence (AI) is expanding eye care beyond image-based detection toward prognosis, treatment-response prediction, monitoring, triage, and clinician-facing decision support. We evaluated AI across eye-disease screening, diagnosis, prognosis, treatment response, and decision support, emphasizing validation, explainability, and clinical readiness. Methods: This PROSPERO-registered review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. Six databases plus supplementary routes identified English-language literature published from 1 January 2015 through 10 August 2026. Included studies underwent design-mapped Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI)/adapted-JBI item-level appraisal; heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis. Results: The evidence base comprised 270 studies. Diabetic retinopathy/diabetic macular oedema was the largest clinical area (82), followed by retinal/multi-disease AI (52), glaucoma (46), and age-related macular degeneration (AMD)/macular disease (29); convolutional neural network (CNN)/convolutional deep learning was the largest primary method group (136). External validation was confirmed in 130 studies, including 95 with a clinical/geographic/prospective/real-world external-validation component (86 clinical-only and nine mixed clinical + technical); 49 had a strict direct clinical comparator and 90 used explainability. Pediatric/pediatric-relevant evidence accounted for 30 studies, while explicit optometry/optometrist involvement appeared in only three. Conclusions: Ophthalmic AI spans diagnosis through clinical management, but translation remains limited by heterogeneous outcomes, incomplete independent validation, few direct comparators, and sparse evaluation of safety, workflow effects, and patient outcomes.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Higher Education Management: Global Applications and Emerging Practices in Vietnam
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming higher education not only through teaching, learning, and scientific research but also through the management and governance of higher education institutions. Universities are beginning to employ AI in admissions, student administration, academic advising, early-warning systems, human-resource management, financial administration, scheduling, quality assurance, institutional planning, communication, and decision support. This development represents a transition from predominantly rule-based and reactive administration toward increasingly data-driven, predictive, and adaptive forms of institutional management. However, the adoption of AI also creates significant challenges concerning data quality, privacy, algorithmic bias, transparency, accountability, institutional autonomy, professional responsibility, and the appropriate boundaries between automated recommendations and human decisions. This article examines the current applications of AI in higher education management internationally and analyses the emerging situation in Vietnam. Drawing on recent international policy literature, empirical research, UNESCO assessments, OECD analysis, and Vietnamese regulatory and research sources, the article argues that AI should not be understood merely as an instrument for administrative automation. Rather, it is becoming an institutional capability that can reshape how universities collect and interpret information, allocate resources, provide services, identify risks, and make strategic decisions. In Vietnam, the policy environment is moving rapidly toward more systematic integration of digital technologies and AI into higher education management. The newly effective Circular No. 49/2026/TT-BGDĐT explicitly regulates the application of digital technologies and AI in higher education, including governance, management, student services, data integration, analysis, forecasting, and decision-making. Nevertheless, institutional readiness remains uneven, and the quality of management information systems and institutional data remains a critical determinant of successful AI adoption. The article proposes a human-centred model of AI-enabled university management based on strategic alignment, data quality, institutional readiness, risk-based deployment, transparency, human oversight, accountability, and continuous evaluation. The article concludes that the future of AI in higher education management should not be defined by the replacement of administrators with algorithms but by the development of institutional intelligence in which AI expands human analytical capacity while universities retain responsibility for educational, ethical, and organizational judgment.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Money Management: A Multidisciplinary Framework for Financial Decision-Making
items.abstract: The rapid integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into financial services has significantly transformed traditional approaches to money management.This study aims to examine the role of AI in enhancing financial decision-making through a multidisciplinary lens, incorporating perspectives from management, behavioural finance, and information technology.Adopting a quantitative research design, primary data were collected through a structured questionnaire administered to individuals actively engaged in financial decision-making.The study investigates key factors influencing the adoption of AI-based money management tools, including perceived usefulness, ease of use, financial literacy, and trust in technology.Using statistical techniques such as regression analysis and structural equation modelling (SEM), the findings reveal that AI-driven tools positively impact financial planning, investment decisions, and overall financial efficiency.The results further indicate that behavioural factors, particularly trust and financial awareness, play a significant mediating role in the effective utilization of AI in money management.The study contributes to the existing literature by proposing a multidisciplinary framework that integrates technological, behavioural, and managerial dimensions of AI adoption in financial contexts.The practical implications of the study highlight the need for financial institutions and policymakers to promote AI literacy and develop user-centric financial technologies to enhance decision-making outcomes.This research offers valuable insights for academicians, practitioners, and policymakers aiming to leverage AI for improved financial management practices.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Pharmaceutical Market Access and Evidence Generation: From Real-World Evidence to Health Technology Assessment and Patient Access — A Scoping Review
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging as a transformative technology in pharmaceutical market access and evidence generation, offering new opportunities to improve healthcare decision-making through advanced data analytics and predictive modelling. The integration of machine learning, natural language processing, deep learning, and generative AI has the potential to strengthen real-world evidence (RWE) generation, health technology assessment (HTA), health economics and outcomes research (HEOR), pricing and reimbursement strategies, and patient access. This scoping review aims to map the applications of AI across the pharmaceutical market access pathway, with particular emphasis on evidence generation, clinical and economic evaluation, and patient-centred healthcare. The review is designed to follow an established scoping review framework and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). Relevant literature is intended to be identified through searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, and Web of Science, supplemented by relevant HTA agency publications. The evidence will be organized according to AI techniques, application areas, reported benefits, implementation challenges, and research gaps. Key areas of interest include AI-assisted analysis of healthcare data, automated evidence synthesis, economic modelling, reimbursement planning, and patient stratification. Despite these opportunities, challenges related to data quality, algorithmic bias, transparency, privacy, model validation, and regulatory acceptance may limit practical implementation. The review aims to identify emerging applications and research priorities while emphasizing the importance of responsible AI governance, methodological rigor, and human oversight. Overall, AI may support more efficient evidence generation and informed pharmaceutical market access decisions; however, its clinical, economic, and societal value requires further empirical evaluation.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Models for Early Disease Detection Using Clinical Data
items.abstract: In a variety of chronic and acute diseases, earlier detection of disease is a major determinant of better patient outcomes, better treatment costs savings and reduced mortality.The current diagnostic process, mostly manual, manual interpretation of clinical data, is limited by the capacity of the human mind, by inter-observer variability and by the amount of data produced by modern healthcare systems.Artificial Intelligence (AI) that leverages machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) capabilities has become a rapidly evolving technology that can help uncover patterns within very large, heterogeneous and high-dimensional clinical datasets, well in advance of what traditional methods could accomplish.In this research paper, a thorough investigation of AI models for early disease detection from medical data, such as laboratory results, electronic health records (EHR), vital signs, and medical image metadata is conducted.We examine the theoretical underpinnings of important classifiers like Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machines, Random Forests, Gradient Boosting methods, Artificial Neural Networks, Convolutional Neural Networks and Long Short-Term Memory networks and compare their performances using the metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC).A systematic procedure of data acquisition, data preprocessing, feature engineering, model training, model validation and interpretability is suggested and illustrated using simulated experiments.The results show that ensemble and deep learning algorithms (especially XGBoost and CNN) are more accurate at forecasting than traditional statistical models, but they are less interpretable and more demanding in terms of resources.The paper also highlights these issues of data privacy, class imbalance, explainability of AI models, and clinical integration, and proposes directions for future research such as federated learning, explainable AI, multimodal data fusion for early disease detection, among others.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Needs Control Theory: Towards Stable, Adaptive, and Autonomous AI Systems
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence systems are increasingly capable of reasoning, planning, and interacting with external tools. However, capability alone does not guarantee stable behavior, reliable execution, or successful task completion under uncertainty and disturbances. This paper investigates how control-theoretic principles can inform the design of more stable, adaptive, and autonomous AI systems. It develops a formal model of the closed cognitive control loop, examines practical stability and actuator gain uncertainty, and introduces the Unified Cognitive Control Framework (UCCF), a proposed architecture integrating state estimation, feedback, adaptation, verification, and safety mechanisms. The framework is evaluated through a simulation-based proof of concept using a controlled navigation task. Across 500 trials per configuration, the full UCCF configuration achieved an 83.8% task success rate, compared with 61.4% for a raw-feedback baseline. These results provide preliminary evidence that combining feedback with additional control and verification mechanisms can improve task performance in the simulated environment. The study also discusses limitations concerning metric validation, model assumptions, computational overhead, and generalization to deployed AI agents. The simulation does not establish equivalent performance improvements in real-world large language model (LLM) agents. This work contributes a control-oriented perspective on autonomous AI system design and outlines a research direction for integrating stability, adaptation, and runtime verification into increasingly capable AI architectures. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence; Control Theory; Autonomous Systems; LLM Agents; Feedback Control; Runtime Verification; Stability; Adaptive Systems. items.title: Artificial Intelligence Policy and Wage Gaps: Evidence from China
items.abstract: A new round of technological revolution centered on artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping the global labor market. Using panel data for 280 Chinese cities from 2011 to 2023, this study treats the establishment of National New-Generation Artificial Intelligence Innovation and Development Pilot Zones (AIIDPZs) as a quasi-natural experiment and employs a staggered difference-in-differences model to examine the impact of AI policy on wage gaps. The results show that the AIIDPZs significantly widen wage gaps within cities. Mechanism tests point to three channels: innovation technology benefit bias, industrial restructuring, and technology diffusion. The effects are stronger in cities in the eastern region, cities with well-developed digital infrastructure, and cities with lower human capital. These findings support incorporating the effects of income distribution into policy evaluation, strengthening skills training and mechanisms for sharing innovation gains, tailoring support to local conditions, and coordinating AI policy with employment policy.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Segmentation In Musculoskeletal Ultrasound
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the performance of an artificial intelligence (AI) technology in recognizing and segmenting anatomical structures across five joints (shoulder, elbow, wrist/hand, knee, and ankle/foot) in musculoskeletal ultrasound (US). DESIGN: This cross-sectional study included 79 adults. Software segmentations were compared to ground truth annotations provided by four experts. Performance was assessed using positive predictive agreement (PPA) and negative predictive agreement (NPA), with a true/false threshold defined as a dice similarity coefficient (DSC) ≥0.50. Subjects with and without sonographic disorders were evaluated to assess robustness. RESULTS: 3017 cine clips (15600 frames) covering 120 anatomical structures were analyzed. PPA and NPA exceeded 0.90 for most structures; tendons, muscles, and nerves showed near-perfect agreement (≥0.97). Similar performance was observed in healthy subjects (PPA: 0.93-0.96; NPA: 0.94-0.99) and subjects with sonographic disorders (PPA: 0.91-0.96; NPA: 0.91-0.99) (P<0.001). CONCLUSION: This first large-scale study demonstrates the high accuracy and reliability of AI-based segmentation. By improving anatomical identification consistency during image acquisition, the software may help reduce technical operator dependency. The results further indicate strong potential for real-time assistance, supporting clinicians and trainees, and underscore the broader applicability of AI-based software in musculoskeletal US.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Supported Teaching Approaches in Nursing Education: A Scoping Review
items.abstract: Background: The increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) has generated growing interest in its use to support teaching and learning in nursing education. This scoping review aimed to map the existing literature on AI-supported teaching approaches in nursing education, examine how learning outcome domains are addressed, and identify gaps in the current evidence base. Method: A scoping review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute Framework and PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Scoping Reviews) guidelines. Eight databases were searched: ProQuest Central, Scopus, ScienceDirect, Web of Science, MEDLINE, Cochrane Library, ERIC, and PubMed. Results: Thirty-eight studies published were included. Three themes emerged: AI tools and applications in nursing education, learning outcome domains and assessment approaches, and current limitations and future directions. Conclusion: AI-supported teaching approaches show promise in nursing education by supporting knowledge and skill development. However, further research using robust designs and clear pedagogical frameworks is needed to inform sustainable educational practice.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Trends for Automatically Identifying Hate Speech on Social Media Networks
items.abstract: The web community views online derision as a threatening issue since it might be detrimental facing people individually as well as to society at large. Social media nevertheless offers a user friendly forum where interested individuals or organizations may openly debate and voice their thoughts regarding relevant issues. In order to identify trends in online speech that detect hate speech tasks, a primary goal of this work is to check recent literature on this subject. The resources utilized for this study were found by searching several databases, like as Google Scholar and ACM Digital Library. The current investigation was undertaken utilising the Preferred Reporting Things for Systematic Assessments and Meta- Analysis (PRISMA) procedure. Multiple records were inspected. From 2020 to 2023, 3500 articles were studied. 3469 were removed due to duplicates and irrelevant databases, and 21 were included. The evaluation indicates that the Supervised Machine learning algorithm was the often-utilized model for classifying nasty texts found online though deep techniques and machine methods have also demonstrated potential in the identification of nasty words on ground nowadays. This study comes to the conclusion that approaches for both machine learning and deep learning have shown promise in the categorization. of slanderous comments on online forums. However, in order to detect and restrict, hostile rhetoric hybrid cross-platform models must be developed.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Personalization and Consumer Engagement: Examining the Future of Customer Experience in the Digital Economy
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven personalization has become a transformative innovation in the digital economy, enabling organizations to deliver tailored products, services, and interactions that enhance customer experience and consumer engagement. As AI technologies, including machine learning, predictive analytics, recommendation systems, and chatbots, become increasingly integrated into digital platforms, understanding their influence on consumer behavior is essential for achieving sustainable competitive advantage. This study examined the effects of artificial intelligence-driven personalization on customer experience, customer satisfaction, and consumer engagement in the digital economy. Specifically, it determined the effect of AI-driven personalization on customer experience, examined the influence of customer experience on customer satisfaction, and assessed the combined effects of AI-driven personalization, customer experience, and customer satisfaction on consumer engagement. A mixed methods research design using the convergent parallel approach was adopted. Quantitative data were collected through a structured questionnaire administered to 400 respondents selected through stratified random sampling, while qualitative data were obtained through semi-structured interviews with 20 purposively selected participants. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, multiple regression, and Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), whereas qualitative data were analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings revealed that artificial intelligence-driven personalization has a significant positive effect on customer experience, customer experience significantly enhances customer satisfaction, and artificial intelligence-driven personalization, customer experience, and customer satisfaction jointly exert significant positive effects on consumer engagement, with AI-driven personalization emerging as the strongest predictor. Qualitative findings further confirmed that personalized recommendations, predictive services, and intelligent digital interactions improve customer experience, increase satisfaction, and foster sustained consumer engagement. The study concludes that AI-driven personalization is a strategic capability for enhancing customer experience and strengthening long-term consumer engagement in the global digital economy. It recommends that organizations invest in AI-driven personalization technologies, adopt customer-centric digital strategies, integrate AI into customer relationship management systems, and promote ethical AI governance, robust digital infrastructure, and effective consumer data protection to achieve sustainable competitiveness.

items.title: Artificial intelligence-Driven Renewable Energy Solutions for Rural Electrification in Africa
items.abstract: This research examines the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in advancing renewable energy solutions for rural electrification in Africa, where energy access remains a critical challenge. The study adopts a qualitative research approach, utilizing secondary data from academic journals, industry reports, and case studies. Comparative analysis is applied to assess AI-driven electrification projects and their effectiveness in rural settings. The paper explores AI technologies such as machine learning, predictive analytics, and smart grid optimization in renewable energy applications like energy demand forecasting, smart grid management, and predictive maintenance. Case studies from Nigeria, Kenya, and South Africa highlight successful implementations of AI in solar mini-grids, wind energy projects, and battery storage solutions. In Nigeria, AI-powered mini-grids optimize energy generation and storage, ensuring consistent power supply in off-grid areas. In Kenya, AI supports wind forecasting and grid management, increasing the efficiency of the Lake Turkana Wind Power Project. In South Africa, AI-driven battery storage systems enhance the reliability of energy distribution by predicting optimal charging and discharging cycles. Despite these advancements, the study identifies challenges such as high initial costs, technical expertise gaps, and regulatory barriers, which hinder scalability. The paper offers recommendations for addressing these challenges, including investment in AI research and development, capacity building, public-private partnerships, and the development of regulatory frameworks. The findings suggest that with targeted investments, policy support, and technological advancements, AI-driven renewable energy solutions can drive rural electrification, contributing to socio-economic development and sustainable energy access in Africa's underserved communities.

items.title: Artificial intelligence-enabled clinical phenotyping of human brown fat
items.abstract: Adipose tissue has a central role in systemic energy balance and the pathogenesis of obesity and its sequelae1,2. In contrast to white adipose tissue, brown adipose tissue (BAT) uses energy to produce heat3. Detectable BAT in humans is associated with decreased prevalence of cardiometabolic diseases4. However, the complete spectrum of health conditions associated with BAT remains unknown, and high-throughput methods to quantify BAT activity in humans are lacking5,6. Here we leveraged big data and artificial intelligence to systematically define the clinical impact of BAT in a cohort of 101,243 patients from a large cancer centre. Our unbiased analyses revealed that, across all diagnoses, cardiovascular and psychiatric diseases were less prevalent in people with BAT. Using a machine learning approach, we semi-automatically quantified BAT activity in approximately 8,700 patients and demonstrated that higher BAT activity, especially in the axillary depot, is associated with lower odds of cardiometabolic diseases and healthier white fat distribution. People with BAT also exhibited more favourable glycaemic parameters, lipid profiles, inflammatory markers and echocardiographic indices. Analysis of medication usage demonstrated that angiotensin receptor blocker use was positively associated with BAT presence. As proof of concept, we showed that the angiotensin receptor blocker losartan increased brown adipocyte activity and whole-body energy expenditure. Altogether, our studies harnessing artificial intelligence and big data identify new clinical phenotypes linked to BAT and serve as a platform for drug repurposing to activate this tissue in humans. Artificial intelligence-enabled quantification and analyses of brown adipose tissue (BAT) activity uncover links between BAT and a healthier metabolic profile along with lower rates of psychiatric disease, and can identify pharmacologic agents that could be repurposed to activate this tissue in humans.
